The hardware did not switch.
`ros_control` or `ros_canopen` is outdated." and later "Please  check that `canopen_motor_node` got updated.
(updating the metapackage does not update the individual packages)" / "I guess you will need  `controller_manager` and `hardware_interface` at least." The reporter confirms the resolution: "updated ``controller_manager`` and ``hardware_interface``solved the problem with the tray" (2017-04-19).

E2.evidence: Step 1: the two units whose interaction failed are canopen_motor_node (ros-industrial/ros_canopen; the process implementing hardware_interface::RobotHW and hosting the controller manager, launched as tray_driver) and ros_control's controller_manager/hardware_interface (ros-controls/ros_control; the library whose ControllerManager reported the switch). Step 2: the failure is between them (the manager reported 'Switched Controllers' while the hardware layer never changed operation mode), so not internal. Step 3: no names were rebound. Step 4: the only resolving change the source documents is installing newer versions of the already-released controller_manager and hardware_interface packages on the robot PC; the thread names no interface element, no API, and no revision of either unit, and the dataset record codes the fault EVOLUTION:PACKAGE ("updating the metapackage does not update the individual packages"). That is a dependency-resolution change with no interface change identified in the source, so the walk stops at step 4 (build). Context not stated in the source but visible in the two projects' changelogs: ros_control 0.9.4 (2016-02-12) "Introduce prepareSwitch, replacement of canSwitch" and "Fix doSwitch execution point"; canopen_motor_node 0.6.5 (2016-12-10) "removed canSwitch implementation, added compile-time check for prepareSwitch" / "moved switch implemenation to non-RT prepareSwitch". A canopen_motor_node release written against ros_control >= 0.9.4 running with a controller_manager < 0.9.4 would never have its prepareSwitch called, which matches 'the hardware did not switch'; but that would be a stale provider (the inverse of UPGRADE) and the installed versions are not stated, so it is recorded here only as a note.

E3.evidence: Not evaluated: the walk stopped at E2 step 4. If the changelog reading above were confirmed, the operation would be a library-API version skew in which the provider (ros_control) is older than the revision the consumer (canopen_motor_node) was built against, which the operation set does not cover.

E4.evidence: Not evaluated (stopped at E2). The effect itself is documented: the tray did not move; candump shows op_mode_display 00 throughout.
